title: CoreDNS unable to forward to Docker's internal DNS
body:
**What happened**:

Since 1.11.4, it's no longer possible to forward to Docker's internal DNS server. 1.11.3 works fine.

**What you expected to happen**:

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

```
. {
    errors
    log

    forward . 127.0.0.11
}
```

```yaml
services:
  coredns:
    image: coredns/coredns:1.11.4
    container_name: coredns
    volumes:
      - ./Corefile:/home/<user>/Corefile:ro
    ports:
      - "53054:53/udp"

  coredns_working:
    image: coredns/coredns:1.11.3
    container_name: coredns_working
    volumes:
      - ./Corefile:/home/<user>/Corefile:ro
    ports:
      - "53053:53/udp"
```

#### Working

```
$ dig coredns @participant7 -p 53053 A +short
172.20.0.3
```

#### Broken

```
$ dig coredns @participant7 -p 53054 A +short
```


**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:

- the version of CoreDNS: 1.11.4 (1.12.0 is also broken)
- Corefile: (as above)
- logs, if applicable:

```
coredns_working  | [INFO] 172.20.0.1:50609 - 28583 "A IN coredns. udp 48 false 1232" NOERROR qr,rd,ra 48 0.000462079s
coredns          | [INFO] 172.20.0.1:50574 - 31747 "A IN coredns. udp 48 false 1232" NOERROR qr,aa,rd 79 0.000182265s
```

- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Linux (Debian and Arch)
- Others:

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I actually think this might be a feature, not a bug (as the best bugs are).

The change which broke my example is actually bf38e4dbd9e5ca2f002f901fad386d97c80b42ce. When the base image was changed, the CWD was changed accidentally to `/home/<user>`. In 1.11.4, the above commit was merged, moving the default back to `/`, and so my above example doesn't actually load the config, and thus doesn't work. Changing the `1.11.4` container to mount its config to `/Corefile` works just fine, as does removing `WORKDIR` from the container.

I think 1.11.4 is working correctly now, as most examples assume `/Corefile` as the configuration file. If anything, an improvement would be to either fail if no config file is found, or changing the default container to explicitly use `/Corefile` for configuration, or at least display which file is being used on startup. 

If changing the args to `/Corefile` is ok, I can get a PR opened.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
> Do you mean to just change `/home/<user>/Corefile` to `/Corefile` in the `compose.yml`?

Yes, did you try it? CoreDNS checking for the config relative to the WORKDIR. Create/mount your Corefile config at the root `/` of the container filesystem.

---

I have a `compose.yaml` example [here](https://github.com/docker-mailserver/docker-mailserver/issues/3520#issuecomment-1700191973) which at the link you can see I integrate with separate `compose.yaml` for connecting/testing with other containers DNS:

```yaml
name: dns-example

networks:
  default:
    name: test-network
    ipam:
      driver: default
      config:
        - subnet: "172.20.42.0/24"

services:
  dns-server:
    image: coredns/coredns:1.12.1
    working_dir: /
    networks:
      default:
        ipv4_address: 172.20.42.10
    configs:
      - source: dns-config
        target: /Corefile
      - source: dns-zone-ptr
        target: /zones/example-rdns.zone
      - source: dns-zone-example
        target: /zones/example-internal.zone

configs:
  dns-config:
    content: |
      # CoreDNS will respond to any reverse DNS queries:
      in-addr.arpa {
        log
        file /zones/example-rdns.zone in-addr.arpa.
      }
      # As well as any DNS queries to `*.example.internal`:
      example.internal {
        log
        file /zones/example-internal.zone example.internal.
      }

      # Delegate queries belonging to these domains to
      # Docker's embedded DNS to resolve to container IP addresses:
      # NOTE: When using `docker compose run`, network aliases are not assigned to the container/DNS,
      # unless explicitly opting in for the container to add those.
      remote.test, example.test {
        log
        forward . 127.0.0.11
      }

      # If you need any other requests to go to public DNS:
      #. {
      #  log
      #  forward . 1.1.1.1
      #}

  # NOTE: `$$` is required to escape `$` from ENV interpolation (Docker Compose feature)
  dns-zone-ptr:
    content: |
      $$TTL 60
      $$ORIGIN 42.20.172.in-addr.arpa.

      @ SOA <redacted-host>. <redacted-host>. 2025102030 4h 1h 14d 10m

      ; Optional - The DNS and DMS containers don't really need PTR records:
      10 PTR <redacted-host>.
      20 PTR mail.example.test.

      30 PTR mail.remote.test.      ; Docker's embedded DNS (127.0.0.11) should have an entry with this IP assigned to the container of this FQDN (hostname).
      40 PTR mail.example.test.     ; This will not resolve back to the same client container IP (the FQDN instead resolves to the IP of the DMS container).
      50 PTR <redacted-host>. ; A valid DNS zone is queried, but there is no `A` record to verify the client IP (NXDOMAIN, non-existent domain).
      60 PTR fail.internal.         ; There is no DNS Zone for `fail.internal`, thus a DNS query will receive no response (timeout, similar to a temporary network error).

      ; Commented out this record to demonstrate what happens when a `PTR` record is missing:
      ; (Otherwise this would be the same as 172.20.42.30, except resolve via CoreDNS instead of Docker)
      ;70.42.20.172.in-addr.arpa. PTR <redacted-host>.

  dns-zone-example:
    content: |
      $$TTL 60
      $$ORIGIN example.internal.

      @ SOA <redacted-host>. <redacted-host>. 2025102030 4h 1h 14d 10m

      ; The IP assigned doesn't need to be valid, but a valid A/MX record is required for passing the restriction `reject_unknown_sender_domain`
      @                       A 172.20.42.10
      ; The primary nameserver referenced by SOA records identify the IP of the authoritative DNS server (the CoreDNS container)
      ns                      A 172.20.42.10
      <redacted-host>. A 172.20.42.70
```

The example above also shows forwarding to Docker's internal DNS is working (_as the linked comment demonstrates_).

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
> so I could remove `WORKINGDIR`

You can't really remove it FWIW, just change it. In this case there is no need to, we want to explicitly override the inherited `WORKDIR` from the base image.

---

By default [`WORKDIR` should be root](https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#workdir) (aka `/`) for any `Dockerfile`, unless it uses a base image that has changed that.

Which is what happened when this projects `Dockerfile` changed the base image from upstream Debian to Google distroless debian non-root. Which was then [corrected by resetting `WORKDIR`](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/6731) in [Oct 2024 for the CoreDNS release v1.11.4](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/commit/bf38e4dbd9e5ca2f002f901fad386d97c80b42ce):

https://github.com/coredns/coredns/blob/1a30dd96953b2c2a216c7244bff74b85f577b737/Dockerfile#L21

---

> ended up going on a whole adventure learning how to build and containerize this just so I could remove `WORKINGDIR`
> and then _also_ made the change to the compose and was grossly confused for a while.

In my earlier `compose.yaml` above, I only explicitly set the `WORKDIR` via equivalent setting so I don't have to think about such issues happening again 😓

```yaml
working_dir: /
```

If you ever run into this situation again with another image, just know that you can change the working directory at runtime via the CLI or `compose.yaml` like this. You don't need to rebuild an image with such changes, that's just for adjusting a default so that you don't need to do it explicitly (_when necessary_).

comments.body: As this issue was regarding an implicit `WORKDIR` change between [`1.11.0`](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/issues/6249#issue-1842444243) and [`1.11.3`](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/issues/7009#issue-2692045531) (_[corrected since `1.11.4`](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/issues/7009#issuecomment-3124851608)_), and that the issue [should not regress again](https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/7428), this issue can now be closed?
